open_points.subject: R0-23 principal-authentication assertion
open_points.text: “whoever acts on the portal does so as one of the three principal types through its own authentication” conflicts with R0-07 and R0-15, which permit the unauthenticated host bootstrap command, staff login, viewer entry, liveness and readiness
open_points.question: Which actions are excluded from R0-23’s assertion that every actor is an authenticated portal principal?
options: The assertion covers only authenticated business operations; bootstrap, authentication-establishing operations and health checks are exceptions
Every request or command must already resolve to one of the three authenticated principal types
open_points.default_guess: Treat bootstrap, login, viewer entry and health checks as explicit exceptions and limit the assertion to authenticated business operations.

witness.initial: The service is running and has no staff accounts.
events: An unauthenticated monitoring system requests readiness.
The host operator invokes the first-administrator command without a portal principal or session.
outcomes: Both actions are allowed under R0-07, R0-11 and R0-15.
Both actions are refused because neither actor is one of the three principal types acting through its own authentication.
witness.observer: The monitoring system and host operator

open_points.subject: Sole-administrator credential recovery
open_points.text: “such a recovery stays a host-level operation outside the product” and “a sole administrator's loss stays the host-level operation of R0-20”
open_points.question: What host-level action exists for a sole administrator who has lost both password and login email, including its actor, authority, inputs, stored changes, observable success, failures and audit treatment?
options: A supported local recovery command changes specified credentials
Direct database or operational intervention is the recovery procedure
No supported recovery action exists and redeployment or data repair is required
open_points.default_guess: Define a separate host-only recovery command with explicit credential inputs and closed success and failure outcomes.

witness.initial: Exactly one active administrator exists and that person no longer knows either the password or the recorded login email.
events: A host operator attempts the recovery that R0-20 and R0-23 say remains outside the product.
outcomes: A defined host operation restores access and reports a specified result.
There is no defined operation, so the operator must guess whether to edit SQLite, create another account, or rebuild the deployment.

open_points.subject: Email-verified mark lifecycle
open_points.text: “A staff account keeps a recorded ‘email verified’ mark: the administrator's activation, the first administrator's creation (R0-07) and the recovery override (R0-20) set it”
open_points.question: What value does the mark have when an ordinary staff account is created, and can any later event clear or otherwise change it?
options: It is a required boolean initially false and becomes permanently true on the named events
It is nullable or absent until one of the named events sets it
It records richer provenance or time rather than a boolean
open_points.default_guess: Use a required boolean initially false, set permanently to true by activation, bootstrap creation or recovery override.

witness.initial: An administrator has just created a staff account in pending_verification state and has not activated it.
events: An authorized actor reads the account before activation.
outcomes: The account view reports email_verified as false.
The account view reports the mark as absent or unknown because no event has set it.

open_points.subject: Account view exposing the email-verified mark
open_points.question: Which concrete account-reading operation shows the mark, and which principal types are allowed to receive that output?
options: Only administrator staff-account detail reads show it
Administrator list and detail reads show it
A staff member's own account view also shows it
Every representation of a staff account shows it
open_points.default_guess: Expose it on administrator-authorized staff-account detail output only.

witness.initial: An active operator account has its email-verified mark set.
events: The operator requests any available self-account representation.
An administrator lists staff accounts and opens that operator's detail.
outcomes: Only the administrator detail output contains the mark.
The self view, list output and administrator detail all contain the mark.

open_points.subject: No-message non-goal
open_points.text: “send email or any other message to a staff member, a client or any address”
open_points.question: Does “any other message” prohibit only outbound notification and delivery channels, or does it also include ordinary HTTP API responses and authenticated binary responses sent to staff and clients?
options: It prohibits email, SMS, push and similar out-of-band delivery but permits API responses and downloads
It literally prohibits every message addressed to staff or clients, including portal responses
open_points.default_guess: Limit the prohibition to outbound notification or delivery channels; ordinary requested HTTP responses remain permitted.

witness.initial: A viewer has a valid session and an active project grant.
events: The viewer requests the project's budget through the HTTP API.
outcomes: The portal returns the promised JSON response because request-response traffic is not a notification message.
The portal cannot return the response because it would be a message sent to a client.
